x: Mitchell’s time was the 6th fastest for his stage, but his performance is better than would be thought at first glance, for among his rivals over this stretch were Beman, Harper, Holden of Tipton H.; Johnston, Herne Hill H ; Bignall, Highgate H.; and Oddie, S.L.H.; all of whom are “internationals.”

Thus at the end of 3 miles the first to appear was Holden, of Tipton; Howard, of Kettering; Beman, Birchfield; and Evenson, of Salford. Our Bert was here definitely 62nd, Warboys 85th, Allum 97th, Bill Webb 101st, Ernie Duffett 128th, Frank Webb 137th and Bill Rice 182nd.

A field of 289 faced the starter, and Bailey, of Salford, made the pace a hot one, with Burns and Holden in close attendance. Bailey led until half-way round the finishing field and then Burns came by him with a great burst to win a magnificent race.

Bailey, of Salford, was leading, followed by Holden (Tipton H.), Evenson (Salford H.), Webster (Birchfield H.), Dodd (Wirrall A.C.), Sutherland (Birchfield H.) and —yes! a Belgrave vest—Penny, seventh.

More by luck that judgment I was well placed in the seventh position, at the end of the first mile, with Bailey (Salford), Holden (Tipton), Evenson (Salford), Webster (Birchfield), Dodd (Wirral A.C.) and Sutherland (Birchfield) in front of me.

At four miles Burns (Elswick) was in the lead, followed by Sutherland (Birchfield), Holden (Tipton), Eaton (Salford), Dodd (Wirral), Robinson (Birchfield), Penny (Belgrave) and Weatherill (S.L.H.) Birchfield were said to have six men in 19 at this point, and we looked certain of a place.

Jack Holden was tucked inside some 15 yards further behind, with Alec Burns not far away. Of ours, Arthur Penny came next, with Tom Evenson and Bert Footer all together at the head of the main bunch, and ours close enough to be "alright."
Bingham trailed Carter, and a few yards behind Bingham came Hoath, who on this lap had moved up to 7th from 13th position. Jack Holden, the oft-times International, was 9th.
Newell ran a fine race to finish runner-up to Holden of Cambridge H. and was always in second or third place and Mike Stearman also ran well to finish in 7th position.

On 20th December, against the local club, Cambridge Harriers, it was unfortunate that our captain, Jack Brown, turned up just too late to take part in the race. Holden, of Cambridge, was first home, followed by Chas.
SIX MILES: Belgrave's ARTHUR PENNY (7) won from Rankine (Canada), Furze (5), Holden(6), Potts (8) and Oliver (Canada) in 31:00.

At seven miles Burns (Elswick) had increased his lead to one of over 100 yards from Holden (Tipton) and Dodd (Wirral), who were together. Penny had shaken off some of his opposition and was now sixth.
10 Victoria Park 5m: Holden of Chelmsford had finished 2nd in a previous year's attempt at this race and was intent on going one place better.
